item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
071
ACPN50 PHFO 271147
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a low pressure area
located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands have become a
little better organized. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development, and a tropical depression is likely to
form over the next days while the system drifts to the northeast,
before turning westward this weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven
NNNN

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...LALA CONTINUES MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWARD... As of 5:00 AM HST Thu Aug 27 the center of Lala was located near 37.2, -178.6 with movement N at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 999 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 271436
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  61
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...LALA CONTINUES MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...37.2N 178.6W
ABOUT 610 MI...980 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 37.2 North, longitude 178.6 West. Lala is 
moving toward the north near 5 mph (7 km/h). A northward to 
north-northwestward motion is expected through today, followed by a 
gradual turn toward the west-northwest tonight and Friday. On the 
forecast track, Lala is forecast to cross the International Date 
line in about 30 h.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low tonight or 
Friday morning.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 61
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 271436
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  61
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
Convection associated with Lala is gradually decreasing, with the 
central convection comprised of some weak bands to the east of the 
center. However, ASCAT and OSCAT scatterometer data indicate that 
the maximum winds remain near 40 kt.

The cyclone is moving northward or 350/4 kt.  A northwestward motion 
is expected for the next day or so, followed by a turn toward the 
west-northwest as Lala becomes embedded in the flow between a 
low-level ridge to the north and a western Pacific tropical cyclone 
approaching from the south. This motion should continue until the 
system dissipates. The new forecast track is similar to the previous 
track.

A combination of cool sea surface temperatures, moderate shear, and 
dry air entrainment should cause Lala to weaken, and the cyclone is 
expected to lose its organized convection and become post-tropical 
between 24-36 h. The remnants of Lala are forecast to weaken to a 
trough between 60-72 h.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
